headline: Ethiopia Plants 47 Billion Seedlings to Restore Its Forests
meta_description: Ethiopia has planted over 47 billion seedlings in seven years, raising forest cover from 17.2% to 23.6% and reversing decades of deforestation.
summary_short: In seven years, Ethiopia planted 47 billion seedlings to restore forests. Forest cover jumped from 17.2% in 2019 to 23.6% in 2023—a remarkable turnaround.
body:
Ethiopia has planted more than 47 billion seedlings over the past seven years, dramatically reversing the country's forest loss and restoring vast areas of degraded land.

The scale of the effort is staggering. In a single day alone, Ethiopia planted 800 million seedlings, showcasing the nation's commitment to large-scale ecological restoration. The results speak for themselves: forest cover rose from just 17.2% in 2019 to 23.6% in 2023, a gain of 6.4 percentage points in four years.

This restoration effort represents more than environmental recovery. It signals a turning point for a nation that has struggled with deforestation for decades. By replanting billions of trees, Ethiopia is rebuilding ecosystems, storing carbon, and creating a foundation for long-term sustainability—one seedling at a time.
quick_facts: 47 billion seedlings planted over seven years
800 million trees planted in a single day
Forest cover increased from 17.2% to 23.6% between 2019 and 2023
